office_does: A State Senator writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes, for a four-year term.
race_blurb: Open seat after Democratic Sen. Sharon Shewmake's retirement. Republican Erika Creydt, a Blaine School Board director, led the primary with about 45%; Democrat Michael Shepard, a Port of Bellingham commissioner, took second by four votes over Eamonn Collins after a hand recount. Creydt campaigns on repealing the 2026 income tax and auditing state spending; Shepard on education funding, abortion rights and limits on federal immigration enforcement.

candidates.summary: Clinical psychologist, counseling-clinic founder and Blaine School Board director running as a Republican on affordability, tax restraint and state spending accountability.
highlights: Calls for repealing the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million enacted under SB 6346 [S5]
Says Washington has a spending problem and programs without measurable results should be reformed or eliminated [S4][S5]
Supports streamlining permitting to increase housing supply while protecting farmland and water [S5]
Opposes the state water adjudication covering about 30,000 Whatcom landowners [S7]

taxes.basis: Repeated explicit opposition to a state income tax and a call to repeal the SB 6346 tax; also criticizes the 2025 services sales tax.

spending.basis: Says the state has a spending problem; would review, reform or eliminate programs without measurable return before any new revenue.

housing.basis: Supply-side approach of streamlining permitting and removing barriers, bounded by infrastructure and farmland protection.

healthcare.basis: Focuses on keeping people insured after federal cuts and addressing provider shortages within the current system.

experience.basis: School board director with no legislative record, running to 'challenge the policies and politicians' in Olympia, against a commissioner backed by the retiring senator.

candidates.summary: Three-term Port of Bellingham commissioner and Western Washington University anthropology faculty member running as a Democrat, endorsed by the retiring senator.
highlights: Voted for a port resolution limiting civil immigration detentions on port property [S14]
Describes himself as "100% pro-choice" and pledges to protect reproductive care providers and health data [S1][S11]
Pledges increased K-12 and early-learning funding [S8]
Proposes a state self-insurance model for Medicare and Medicaid [S4][S15]
Opposes "defund the police" and says law enforcement needs more resources [S6]

immigration.basis: Voted to bar warrantless civil immigration detentions and detention facilities on port property and says he is proud of that vote.

social.basis: Says he is '100% pro-choice' and backs abortion and birth-control access and protections for providers; no LGBTQ+ position found.

spending.basis: Pledges increased K-12 and early childhood funding and investment from Pre-K through postsecondary education.

climate.basis: Adopted a port net-zero-by-2050 Climate Action Plan and says the state must keep reducing emissions, while avoiding extra costs on families.

safety.basis: Opposes 'defund the police' and says law enforcement needs more resources; also backs homelessness prevention.

housing.basis: Combines cutting red tape and density near transit with workforce-housing incentives and support for a low-income housing project.

healthcare.basis: Would lower drug prices and expand coverage options and proposes state self-insurance for Medicare and Medicaid, not single-payer.

experience.basis: Nine years as an elected port commissioner, endorsed by the retiring senator and Democratic legislative leaders; no legislative record.
